subject: design-technology
title: Vacuum Forming a Plastic Shell Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says the vacuum sucks and pulls the soft plastic sheet down onto the mould. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - the vacuum pulls the sheet down
The vacuum only removes the air beneath the sheet, and unopposed outside air pressure pushes the pliable sheet onto the mould.
The heater pushes the sheet down onto the mould
The mould sucks the sheet down onto itself

questions.misconception: The vacuum sucks and pulls the soft plastic sheet down onto the mould.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: The vacuum sucks and pulls the soft plastic sheet down onto the mould. Reteach point: The flat sheet is clamped in the frame and heated until pliable, the mould rises into the soft sheet, the vacuum then removes the air trapped beneath it, and the unopposed outside air pressure pushes the sheet onto every surface of the mould, where it cools, sets rigid, and is lifted off and trimmed.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain what the vacuum pump does at the forming stage.
questions.answer: The vacuum pump removes the air trapped beneath the pliable sheet, leaving outside air pressure unopposed.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names removal, not pulling: with the air gone from beneath, outside pressure can push the sheet onto the mould.

questions.prompt: At the heating stage, what has happened to the sheet?

choices.text: It has cooled and set rigid on the mould
It has become pliable and sags under its own weight, ready to be formed
It has already been trimmed into a finished shell
It has been pushed onto every surface of the mould

questions.feedback: Scene 2 shows heating: the sheet softens and sags pliable, but it is not formed until air is removed and pressure pushes it onto the mould.

questions.prompt: State the final stage of the cycle and say why the shell keeps its shape afterwards.
questions.answer: The formed sheet cools on the mould and sets rigid, so the lifted-off, trimmed shell keeps the shape of the mould.
questions.feedback: Credit the cooling reasoning: the plastic must set rigid on the mould before release, or the shell would not keep the mould shape.
